items.title: COVID-19 Queries: Altered DNA and Microchips
items.snippet_en: Mayo Clinic states that assertions about COVID-19 vaccines containing microchips for tracking or gathering personal information are false. This myth originated from comments made by Bill Gates about a digital certificate of vaccine records, not a microchip tied to vaccine development.

items.title: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) myths
items.snippet_en: Mayo Clinic states that assertions about COVID-19 vaccines containing microchips for tracking or gathering personal information are false.

items.title: COVID-19 Vaccines Don’t Have Patient-Tracking Devices
items.snippet_en: FactCheck.org debunks the claim, explaining that a chip discussed by a medical device company executive was for tracking vaccine doses, not people, and would be attached to the vial, not injected.

items.title: HOAKS: Vaksin Covid-19 Memiliki Chip yang Dapat Melacak Keberadaan Orang
items.snippet_en: Indonesian government sources state that the claim of microchips in vaccines for tracking people is false. They clarify that barcodes on vaccine products are for tracking distribution and do not get implanted into individuals.

items.title: Vaksin Covid-19 Memiliki Chip yang Dapat Melacak Keberadaan Orang yang Telah Disuntikan Vaksin
items.snippet_en: Indonesian government sources state that the claim of microchips in vaccines for tracking people is false.
Experts and medical professionals consistently affirm that it is impossible to put tracking microchips in COVID-19 vaccines due to size and technological limitations.
